coverage: All forty-two scenes in both original-en and modern-en: named cast, speaking and stage roles, the client kings and captains of the two rolls, the Roman past behind the action, and the gods and legendary figures named in the play.

entities.name: Mark Antony
entities.body: One of the three rulers of the Roman world, kept in Egypt by Cleopatra.

snapshots.body: One of the three rulers of the Roman world, now married to Octavius Caesar’s sister Octavia.

entities.name: Cleopatra
entities.body: The Queen of Egypt, and Antony’s lover.

snapshots.body: The Queen of Egypt, a prisoner in her own monument.

entities.name: Octavius Caesar
entities.body: The youngest of the three rulers of the Roman world, and Antony’s partner in it.

entities.name: Domitius Enobarbus
entities.body: Antony’s closest officer and the plainest speaker in his following.

snapshots.body: Antony’s old officer, now in Octavius Caesar’s camp.

entities.name: Charmian
entities.body: One of Cleopatra’s attendants, and the closest to her.

entities.name: Sextus Pompeius
entities.body: The son of Pompey the Great, in arms at sea against the three rulers.

entities.name: Lepidus
entities.body: The third of the three rulers of the Roman world, and the weakest of them.

entities.name: Menas
entities.body: A pirate captain in Sextus Pompeius’s service.

entities.name: Eros
entities.body: Antony’s servant and armour-bearer.

entities.name: Agrippa
entities.body: One of Octavius Caesar’s chief officers.

entities.name: Dolabella
entities.body: One of Octavius Caesar’s officers, sent to attend Cleopatra.

entities.name: Iras
entities.body: One of Cleopatra’s attendants.

entities.name: Alexas
entities.body: An attendant on Cleopatra, who carries her messages to Antony.

entities.name: Maecenas
entities.body: One of Octavius Caesar’s counsellors.

entities.name: Octavia
entities.body: Octavius Caesar’s sister, married to Antony to bind the two men together.

snapshots.body: Octavius Caesar’s sister, now married to Antony.

entities.name: Scarus
entities.body: An officer in Antony’s army, wounded fighting for him.

entities.name: Thidias
entities.body: Octavius Caesar’s messenger to Cleopatra, whipped for his pains.

entities.name: Canidius
entities.body: Antony’s lieutenant-general on land.

entities.name: Proculeius
entities.body: An officer of Octavius Caesar’s, whom Antony tells Cleopatra to trust.

entities.name: Mardian
entities.body: A eunuch in Cleopatra’s household.

entities.name: Diomedes
entities.body: An attendant on Cleopatra, sent after Antony with her message.

entities.name: Dercetus
entities.body: A soldier of Antony’s who takes his sword to Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: Ventidius
entities.body: An officer of Antony’s, victorious against the Parthians.

entities.name: Silius
entities.body: An officer serving under Ventidius in Syria.

entities.name: Seleucus
entities.body: Cleopatra’s treasurer, who betrays what she has kept back.

entities.name: Gallus
entities.body: An officer of Octavius Caesar’s, sent with Proculeius to the monument.

entities.name: Taurus
entities.body: Octavius Caesar’s lieutenant-general on land at Actium.

entities.name: Menecrates
entities.body: A pirate captain with Menas in Sextus Pompeius’s service.

entities.name: Varrius
entities.body: A follower of Sextus Pompeius who brings him news of Antony.

entities.name: Philo
entities.body: A follower of Antony’s, who opens the play deploring his change.

entities.name: Demetrius
entities.body: A follower of Antony’s, to whom Philo speaks.

entities.name: The Soothsayer
entities.body: The Egyptian soothsayer who reads the women’s fortunes and warns Antony off Caesar.

entities.name: The Clown
entities.body: The countryman who brings Cleopatra the asps in a basket of figs.

entities.name: The Ambassador
entities.body: Antony’s schoolmaster, sent as his ambassador to Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: The messenger
entities.body: The messenger who brings Cleopatra news of Antony from Rome.

entities.name: The Second Messenger
entities.body: A second messenger bringing news to Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: The soldier
entities.body: A soldier of Antony’s who urges him to fight by land.

entities.name: The First Soldier
entities.body: A soldier on watch in Antony’s camp.

entities.name: The Second Soldier
entities.body: A soldier on watch in Antony’s camp.

entities.name: The Third Soldier
entities.body: A soldier on watch in Antony’s camp.

entities.name: The Fourth Soldier
entities.body: A soldier on watch in Antony’s camp.

entities.name: The Sentry
entities.body: The sentry who finds Enobarbus in Caesar’s camp.

entities.name: The First Watch
entities.body: A watchman with the sentry in Caesar’s camp.

entities.name: The Second Watch
entities.body: A watchman with the sentry in Caesar’s camp.

entities.name: The First Guard
entities.body: A guard at Cleopatra’s monument.

entities.name: The Second Guard
entities.body: A guard at Cleopatra’s monument.

entities.name: The First Servant
entities.body: A servant at Pompey’s galley feast.

entities.name: The Second Servant
entities.body: A servant at Pompey’s galley feast.

entities.name: The servant
entities.body: A servant announcing a messenger to Cleopatra.

entities.name: The Egyptian
entities.body: The Egyptian sent from Cleopatra to Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: The attendants
entities.body: The attendants of the Egyptian court and the Roman camps.

entities.name: The soldiers
entities.body: The soldiers of the Roman and Egyptian armies.

entities.name: The guard
entities.body: Antony’s guard, and the guards set on Cleopatra’s monument.

entities.name: The servants
entities.body: The servants at Pompey’s galley feast.

entities.name: The officers
entities.body: The officers of the two armies.

entities.name: The captains
entities.body: The captains of the two armies.

entities.name: The ladies
entities.body: The ladies of Cleopatra’s court.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman conqueror, Octavius Caesar’s adoptive father, and Cleopatra’s lover before Antony.

entities.name: Pompey the Great
entities.body: Sextus Pompeius’s father, defeated by Julius Caesar at Pharsalia.

entities.name: Gnaeus Pompey
entities.body: Pompey the Great’s elder son, named by Antony among Cleopatra’s earlier lovers.

entities.name: Fulvia
entities.body: Antony’s first wife, who made war on Octavius Caesar and dies early in the play.

entities.name: Lucius
entities.body: Antony’s brother, who joined Fulvia’s war against Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: Caesarion
entities.body: Cleopatra’s son, whom Egypt calls Julius Caesar’s.

entities.name: Alexander
entities.body: Antony and Cleopatra’s son, given Media, Parthia and Armenia at the enthronement.

entities.name: Ptolemy
entities.body: Cleopatra’s brother and husband, dead before the play begins; she is called his queen.

entities.name: Ptolemy
entities.body: Antony and Cleopatra’s son, given Syria, Cilicia and Phoenicia at the enthronement.

entities.name: Marcus Crassus
entities.body: The Roman general the Parthians killed, whom Ventidius avenges.

entities.name: Marcus Octavius
entities.body: One of Antony’s captains at Actium; not Octavius Caesar.

entities.name: Marcus Justeius
entities.body: One of Antony’s captains at Actium.

entities.name: Publicola
entities.body: One of Antony’s captains at Actium.

entities.name: Caelius
entities.body: One of Antony’s captains at Actium.

entities.name: Pacorus
entities.body: King Orodes’s son, killed by Ventidius in Parthia.

entities.name: Orodes
entities.body: The Parthian king, Pacorus’s father.

entities.name: Labienus
entities.body: The Roman who led a Parthian army into Asia against Antony.

entities.name: Sossius
entities.body: An officer of Antony’s in Syria, cited by Ventidius as a warning.

entities.name: Photinus
entities.body: A eunuch named in Rome among those said to manage Cleopatra’s affairs.

entities.name: Herod
entities.body: Herod of Jewry, a client king whose homage Cleopatra imagines and whose allegiance Alexas fails to keep.

entities.name: Bocchus
entities.body: The king of Libya, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Archelaus
entities.body: The king of Cappadocia, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Philadelphos
entities.body: The king of Paphlagonia, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Adallas
entities.body: The Thracian king, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Manchus
entities.body: The king of Arabia, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Mithridates
entities.body: The king of Comagene, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Polemon
entities.body: The king of Mede, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Amyntas
entities.body: The king of Lycaonia, among the kings Antony assembles.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: One of Julius Caesar’s assassins, killed at Philippi.

entities.name: Cassius
entities.body: One of Julius Caesar’s assassins, killed at Philippi.

entities.name: Isis
entities.body: The Egyptian goddess, whose habit Cleopatra wears and whose name she swears by.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The hero Antony claims descent from, and whose music leaves him.

entities.name: Jupiter
entities.body: The king of the gods, also called Jove.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The queen of the gods.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The goddess of love, whose picture Cleopatra outdoes on the Cydnus.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The god of war.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The god of the sea.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: The sun god, whose pinches Cleopatra says have blackened her.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: Fortune as the power that turns men’s luck.

entities.name: Atlas
entities.body: The titan who holds up the world; Cleopatra calls Antony the demi-Atlas of the earth.

entities.name: Telamon
entities.body: Ajax Telamon, who ran mad for Achilles’ armour, in Cleopatra’s picture of Antony’s rage.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: The queen of Carthage, whom Antony imagines walking with Aeneas in the fields of the dead.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: Dido’s lover, named beside her.

entities.name: Narcissus
entities.body: The youth of the myth, in Cleopatra’s abuse of the messenger.

entities.name: Gorgon
entities.body: The monster whose look turned men to stone, in Cleopatra’s figure for Antony.
